title: AI Alignment Is Neither Solvable nor Sufficient
abstract: arXiv:2611.13167v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Humans and AI systems increasingly act within the same social and economic environments. Alignment, the goal of ensuring that AI systems act in accordance with human values, is widely regarded as a central challenge for ensuring that AI benefits society while avoiding harm. We argue that this endeavor is misguided. First, alignment is not well defined, as it presumes a sufficiently stable and identifiable set of human intentions or values. Second, where a concrete notion of alignment can be specified, it is not solvable. Third, where alignment appears solvable, solving it would not necessarily mitigate the negative consequences of AI. A key reason is that alignment is typically framed as a property of individual AI systems, while the resulting hybrid societies of humans and machines are complex systems shaped by interactions and feedback loops. translated_title: AI对齐既无法解决也非充分之道
translated_abstract: 人类与AI系统越来越多地在相同的社会和经济环境中行动。对齐，即确保AI系统的行为符合人类价值观的目标，被广泛认为是确保AI造福社会并避免危害的核心挑战。我们认为这一努力是误入歧途的。首先，对齐没有良好的定义，因为它假定存在一个足够稳定且可辨识的人类意图或价值观集合。其次，在可以具体定义对齐概念的情况下，它是不可解的。第三，在看似可以解决对齐问题的情况下，解决它也不一定会减轻AI的负面影响。一个关键原因是，对齐通常被框定为单个AI系统的属性，而由此形成的人机混合社会却是由互动和反馈回路塑造的复杂系统。因此，涌现的风险，而不仅仅是由个别未对齐系统带来的风险——很可能会（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文论证AI对齐这一目标存在根本缺陷：对齐定义不清、无法求解，且即使实现对齐也不足以化解风险，因为真正需要应对的是人机混合社会这一复杂系统中产生的涌现性风险。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that AI alignment is ill-defined, unsolvable, and insufficient even if achieved, because the real dangers lie in emergent risks arising from complex human-AI hybrid societies rather than in individual misaligned systems.
